mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days because it reflects accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for equity valuation.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in periods of low FEDFUNDS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it signals an economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 4.5%), or the Rank IC for UNRATE in the triggered set is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 3 months signals an imminent recession, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in GDPC1 and INDPRO fails to predict negative returns in > 60% of instances (i.e., 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases when both series decline).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle (FEDFUNDS declining), the reduction in interest rates lowers the cost of capital for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in monetary easing cycles are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days because it indicates robust consumer spending and economic expansion.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in periods of high HOUST are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 320, it signals accelerating inflation that may prompt aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 320), or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL in the triggered set is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) over the past 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative returns in > 60% of instances (i.e., 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases when both conditions hold).

mechanism_narrative: In a period of industrial contraction (INDPRO declining), the reduction in manufacturing output signals weakening economic activity, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in periods of declining INDPRO are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
